Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a packet with the requested snapshots and an excerpt from our DR runbook. Quick notes up front:

- RTO/RPO: Hosted API (multi-tenant) targets are RTO = 5 minutes for control-plane failover; RPO = 0-2 minutes for in-flight token state depending on sequence length (KV cache replication). Dedicated reservations (single-tenant pools) default to RTO = 10 minutes, RPO = 0-5 minutes; we can tighten these under contractual SLAs — I included the SLA matrix in the packet.

- DR tests: Attached are the recovery-test-summary-20260528.csv (last full failover rehearsal) and a high-level writeup of the April exercise. Both show successful failover with warm-cache rebuild times matching our RTO targets.

- Offsite backups: Customer metadata (non-PHI) is persisted to encrypted object storage in a second-region bucket (us-west-2 to us-east-1) with a 90-day retention default; snapshots are retained for 365 days when customers opt-in. Key material uses KMS and is not stored in plaintext.

- Runbook excerpt: See DR_runbook_excerpt.txt — I redacted internal pager numbers but left the escalation chain and step list intact.

Attachments: [BCP_RTO_RPO_snapshot_20260601.pdf], [DR_runbook_excerpt.txt], [recovery-test-summary-20260528.csv]

If you need signed attestations or SOC2-specific control IDs mapped to these artifacts, Monica (CC) handles compliance artifacts and can route formal evidence.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call — I'm free after 1 PM PT today otherwise Monday morning.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Continuity validation for Redwood integration - RTO/RPO and DR evidence

Alex — quick technical answers below (copying Diego and Monica for compliance context):

1) KV cache RPO for chat sessions: We maintain synchronous or near-synchronous replication of the KV cache across two availability zones within a region. For hosted API the effective operational RPO for chat context is < 2 minutes — in practice it's usually sub-30s for active sessions because of continuous prefix/KV checkpointing. For Dedicated pools we offer asynchronous cross-zone replication by default; customers who need sub-30s RPO can enable synchronous replication in the reservation configuration.

2) Dedicated SLA addendum: Yes — we have an SLA addendum that enumerates RTO/RPO per capacity tier and credits for missed targets. Monica will share the redlined addendum PDF and the page that maps capacity tiers to RTO/RPO.

3) Customer-facing restores: We performed two customer data restores in the last 12 months — both were configuration/metadata restores (no model weights or raw customer PII). One in Jan 2026 due to an accidental configuration deletion (restored within 4 hours, root cause documented), and a second in Mar 2026 to recover a corrupted job history (restored within 2 hours). I attached a one-page summary in the recovery-test CSV.

If you want, we can run a short joint session (30 minutes) to walk through the addendum and runbook — propose Tuesday 10:00 AM PT?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
